item.name: Verdant Valley
item.notableEvomon: First wild catches; the opening zone right after the tutorial portal.
item.cardSummary: The first open island after the tutorial. Wild Evomon and the boss lean Rock and Ground, so a Grass, Ground or Water starter has the early edge here.

item.name: Petal Pond
item.notableEvomon: Mostly Normal-type wild Evomon; hosts the EXP challenge for fast leveling.
item.cardSummary: The second island, full of Normal-type Evomon and home to the EXP challenge area that players use to level quickly. The boss Clamspire is Water-type.

item.name: Lava Crag
item.notableEvomon: Fire-themed island where a Water-focused team holds a strong type advantage.
item.cardSummary: The third island and the first big difficulty step. It is Fire-themed, so a Water team dominates both the wild Evomon and the boss Empixy King.

item.name: Amber Acres
item.notableEvomon: Grass-leaning zone where an all-Water team starts to struggle.
item.cardSummary: The fourth island, where the Grass-type wild Evomon and boss Datunymph King punish a pure Water team. Pro Game Guides suggests adding Fire coverage by this point.

item.name: Shiver Snows
item.cardSummary: The fifth island and the start of the mid-game. It is Ice-themed, so Fire and Rock coverage helps against the boss Glacitadel.

item.name: Raven Ridge
item.notableEvomon: Bluebird can spawn at a sky spot reached by climbing the vines around the area.
item.cardSummary: A mid-game island whose boss Volcrest King stacks attack buffs each turn, so the fight gets harder the longer it runs. A confirmed in-game zone name.

item.name: Flying Territory
item.notableEvomon: Defeating the boss here ('King of Flying') unlocks Sundercrene as a flying mount for faster travel.
item.cardSummary: An aerial zone where beating the boss grants the Sundercrene flying mount. NOTE: 'Flying Territory' may be a descriptive label rather than the real in-game zone name and must be verified before publish.

item.name: Silent Sands
item.notableEvomon: Home to the Equipment Dungeon, which unlocks around Level 40 for gear farming.
item.cardSummary: A desert island known for its Equipment Dungeon, a gear-farming activity that opens earlier (around Lv 40) than the island's boss Gearforged King.

item.name: Crystal Cascade
item.notableEvomon: Frostlet becomes available once the zone boss is cleared.
item.cardSummary: A late-game island gated behind the boss Frostseer King. Clearing it opens access to catches like Frostlet.

item.name: Canyon Oasis
item.cardSummary: A late-game (Level 90+ recommended by some guides) island gated by the boss Chitgladi King.

item.name: Murkwood
item.cardSummary: A late-game island guarded by the boss Viparch King, recommended for high-level teams.

item.name: Nether Land
item.cardSummary: A late-game island whose boss Rosastar King is called out as especially tough, dealing enhanced damage after the fourth turn.

item.name: Rocky Ridge
item.cardSummary: A high-level island gated behind the boss Spikumane King, near the end of the current progression route.

item.name: Thunder Cliffs
item.notableEvomon: Thunder Cliffs boss drops Arcub; the highest-level progression island currently documented.
item.cardSummary: The final documented progression island, capped by the Level 200 King of Thunder. Its boss drops Arcub, making it a key late-game farm.
